Hearth & Grain

A wood-fired neighborhood bakery on Alder Street. Every loaf leaves the oven door in crust brown #6B3A2A paper bags stamped with a butter gold #E8A93C wheat sheaf, stacked on flour cream #FFF4E2 shelves beside rye green #4A5A3A window boxes.

The morning bake gallery

Each day the loaves are photographed before the doors open — a photo collection of crusts, crumb, and flour dust pinned to the gallery wall by the counter. The visual study grows one loaf at a time; this week's sheet shows sixteen.

Today's bread

  • Country Sourdough · 48-hour ferment, stone-milled flour · 8 dollars
  • Honey Oat Porridge Loaf · rolled oats, wildflower honey · 7 dollars
  • Seeded Rye · caraway, molasses, cracked rye · 9 dollars
  • Fig and Walnut Batard · dried figs, toasted walnuts · 10 dollars
  • Olive Fougasse · kalamata, rosemary, flake salt · 9 dollars
  • Sesame Semolina · golden sesame, durum · 8 dollars
  • Spelt Bloomer · whole spelt, sunflower seeds · 9 dollars
  • Sourdough Baguette · overnight poolish · 6 dollars
  • Rye and Raisin · dark rye, sultanas · 8 dollars
  • Lemon Drizzle Loaf · candied lemon, icing · 7 dollars
  • Cardamom Knot · cardamom sugar, orange zest · 5 dollars
  • Morning Bun · laminated dough, cinnamon · 5 dollars
  • Almond Croissant · frangipane, toasted flakes · 6 dollars
  • Cinnamon Cruffin · cruffin dough, cinnamon sugar · 6 dollars
  • Celebration Cake · custom lettering, buttercream, per 10-inch tier · 42 dollars
  • Weekday Lunch Slice · soup of the day and sourdough · 11 dollars

Getting your bread

Ask at the counter the evening before for a 7 AM slot from the oven door. Whole loaves only on Saturdays — the wood oven rests on Mondays. Standing weekly baskets for cafés on the same block save 10 percent.

Hours

The counter opens 7 AM to 4 PM, Tuesday through Sunday. First Saturday of each month is kids' shaping day at 9 AM — flour guaranteed everywhere.

Wholesale

Cafés, supper clubs, and the farmers market co-op can set up a weekly basket — hello@hearthandgrain.example. Last quarter 320 loaves went to the food bank from the Saturday surplus list.

Millbrook — 2026 City Budget Report

The proposed budget for the fiscal year beginning July 1, 2026, published for public comment by the Millbrook finance committee. Posters at the library carry the civic navy #1F3A5F header band, brass gold #C9A227 figures, and paper cream #F2EFE6 backgrounds with slate blue #5E718A footnotes.

Where the money goes

  • Road resurfacing and bridges — $4,800,000
  • Water main replacement — $2,300,000
  • Fire and emergency response — $3,100,000
  • Library and community rooms — $640,000
  • Parks and tree planting — $890,000
  • Bus service expansion — $1,150,000

Compare: 2025 versus 2026

Compare the adopted 2025 budget of $11,200,000 with the proposed 2026 budget of $12,700,000 — a 13 percent increase. Per resident, spending rises from $918 to $1,024 across an estimated 12,400 residents. Debt service falls 6 percent.

Timeline of the budget cycle

  • March 3, 2026 — draft published for public comment
  • April 21, 2026 — town hall on the paving and water plan
  • June 30, 2026 — council vote
  • July 1, 2026 — fiscal year begins
  • February 2027 — mid-year review

How the plan was surveyed

The priorities come from a resident survey: 3,050 responses, 61 percent naming road repair first, 22 percent naming the bus expansion. Crossing guards, gutter work, and the fire station roof round out the statistics appendix. Questions go to finance@millbrook.example.

A Texas notebook

A few notes on Texas — the state, the flag, and the people. Kept plain.

Places

  • Alamo, San Antonio (1836)

    A small stone mission at the center of the Texas Republic. Nineteen days, one long siege, one story that carried a state.

  • Big Bend, west Texas (1944)

    Eight hundred thousand acres along the Rio Grande. Cottonwood, prickly pear, and one of the darkest night skies in North America.

  • Austin, on the Colorado (1839)

    Live music, live oaks, live legislature. Named after Stephen F. Austin, the empresario who first brought settlers under Mexican rule.

Signals

  • Lone Star flag (1839)

    Blue for loyalty, white for purity, red for bravery. One five-point star. The only US state flag that once flew over a sovereign republic.

  • Bluebonnet (1901)

    State flower. Only blooms in spring, only along the highway shoulders and the pastures where the ranchers let it.

  • Longhorn (1995)

    State large mammal. Named for the horns, which can reach seven feet from tip to tip. A living remnant of the Spanish criollo cattle.

Contact

Email: notes@texasnote.example.

Now

Rereading J. Frank Dobie. Watching the mockingbird nest under the eave.

A few notes on Texas — the state, the flag, and the people. Kept plain.

Places

  • Alamo, San Antonio (1836)

    A small stone mission at the center of the Texas Republic. Nineteen days, one long siege, one story that carried a state.

    Live music, live oaks, live legislature. Named after Stephen F. Austin, the empresario who first brought settlers under Mexican rule.

Signals

  • Lone Star flag (1839)

    Blue for loyalty, white for purity, red for bravery. One five-point star. The only US state flag that once flew over a sovereign republic.

  • Bluebonnet (1901)

    State flower. Only blooms in spring, only along the highway shoulders and the pastures where the ranchers let it.

  • Longhorn (1995)

    State large mammal. Named for the horns, which can reach seven feet from tip to tip. A living remnant of the Spanish criollo cattle.
